title: Animal Roles — Lion, Lamb, Shepherd, Ox/Cow, Red Heifer, Goat, Serpent, Eagle and Dog
purpose: Populate the animal-role layer by function and source so stacked project identities do not erase distinct textual meanings or become labels for real people.
master_rule: Animal symbol ≠ person essence. Store source, role/function and context on the relation. A single figure may carry several animal metaphors without the animals becoming equivalent.

roles.scholarly_note: Revelation's lion/lamb relation is debated; the text's shift from announced Lion to seen slain Lamb is central to interpretation.

roles.distinction: Lamb is not merely weakness; Revelation weaponizes the paradox of conquest through the slain Lamb.
Shepherd is an office/relationship; sheep/flock are not therefore passive property in every project use.
Do not collapse literal cow, ox, lolcow, cash cow, Holy Cow, Red Heifer, Golden Calf or project Cow-target into one symbol. Each has a different source and function.

cow_subtypes.unholy_cow: project shadow label, not a historical category
cow_subtypes.red_heifer: Numbers 19 purification role; distinct owner retained
cow_subtypes.golden_calf: idolatry/false-center motif; not the same as Cow-as-victim or Red Heifer
cow_subtypes.cow_target: relational target/harvest role that can end through declassification and exit

functions: production of ash used with fresh/living water for corpse-impurity purification
roles.paradox: Participants producing/administering the purifying substance can themselves become temporarily impure.
roles.distinction: Not a generic cow, not simply sacrifice, and not automatically messianic.

functions: paired-goat ritual differentiating offering to YHWH and live goat sent to Azazel/wilderness bearing iniquities
roles.distinction: 'Scapegoat' is a ritual role, not proof that the goat is morally guilty or demonic.

functions: adversarial cosmic imagery in later texts
roles.distinction: Biblical serpents, kuṇḍalinī, caduceus and project serpent are separate lineages.
Eagle does not simply mean Father across all biblical contexts.

source_families: frequent insult/exclusion imagery in biblical texts
functions: biblical contexts often emphasize scavenging, contempt or boundary-outsider status; modern project uses patrol/pursuit/following/guardian roles
roles.distinction: Project Dog is a contextual relational role. Recovered stories show Dogs can guard, chase, orbit, confess, learn, seek Source, change masters or cross toward another state; no single negative function defines the whole family.

tetramorph_bridge.pattern: Ezekiel/Revelation living-creature tradition brings human, lion, ox/calf and eagle faces/forms into one throne-chariot vision complex.
tetramorph_bridge.project_use: Useful for differentiating four functions around a mobile throne/chariot without turning them into a single animal identity.

role_tests: Is this animal the subject, sacrifice, guide, carrier, predator, purifier, outsider, ruler or visionary creature?
Does the source text assign moral value, or are we importing it later?
Is the animal role temporary/contextual or treated as identity?
What changes if the same figure carries another animal symbol in a different passage?
